message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/c-blosc2 && grep -rn "BLOSC2_VERSION_FORMAT_ALPHA\|BLOSC2_MAX_FILTERS\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_VERSION\b\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_FLAGS\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_TYPESIZE\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_NBYTES\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_BLOCKSIZE\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_CBYTES\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_BLOSC2_FLAGS\|BLOSC_MIN_HEADER_LENGTH\|BLOSC_EXTENDED_HEADER_LENGTH\|BLOSC2_CHUNK_VERSIONLZ" blosc/blosc2.h blosc/*.h | head -40

message.content:
Now I understand the vulnerability. In `initialize_context_decompression`, when the extended header is used (both DOSHUFFLE and DOBITSHUFFLE flags set), the code reads `max_filters` filters. For `header_version == BLOSC2_VERSION_FORMAT_ALPHA`, `max_filters = 5`, otherwise `max_filters = BLOSC2_MAX_FILTERS`.

The issue is that `context->filters[i]` and `context->filters_meta[i]` are only set for `i < max_filters`. If `max_filters < BLOSC2_MAX_FILTERS`, the remaining entries in `context->filters` and `context->filters_meta` are uninitialized.

Then in `blosc_d`, `last_filter(filters, 'd')` iterates over all `BLOSC2_MAX_FILTERS` entries, reading uninitialized values. This is the use-of-uninitialized-value.
